output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: multiple call sites did Class.forName(attackerString).newInstance() (or Constructor(String,String).newInstance()) and only checked the expected base type via an implicit cast AFTER construction, so the attacker's constructor (and any side effects: file writes, network calls, JNDI, static initializers) had already executed by the time the ClassCastException surfaced and was swallowed.

Fix: added MappingUtil.loadClass(String className, Class<T> expectedType) which does Class.forName/classLoader.loadClass, then checks expectedType.isAssignableFrom(rawClazz) and throws IllegalArgumentException immediately if not assignable — no instance is ever created for a class outside the expected type. This is now the single choke point used at every flip-strategy sink (MappingUtil.instanceFlippingStrategy, XmlParser.parseFlipStrategy, PropertiesParser.parseFeatures, YamlParser.parseFlipStrategy, ConsoleOperations.createFeature/updateFlippingStrategy) with expectedType=FlippingStrategy.class, and inside PropertyFactory.createProperty(String,String,String,String,Set) with expectedType=Property.class for property-type construction (which XmlParser, PropertiesParser and YamlParser's property-type parsing now delegate to instead of duplicating their own Class.forName+getConstructor logic).

Out of scope / intentionally not touched: ConsoleServlet.init / FF4jServlet.init load an FF4jProvider class from a servlet init-param (deployment-time trust boundary, configured by the application owner via web.xml, not runtime attacker input) — different threat model from the alert's traces. PropertyClass.fromString does Class.forName(v) but never calls newInstance() — it stores the resolved Class object itself as the property's value by design, not a construction sink, so it is not CWE-094.

Removed now-unreachable `catch (ClassNotFoundException e)` clauses in ConsoleOperations where Class.forName was replaced by MappingUtil.loadClass (which throws unchecked IllegalArgumentException instead), and dropped now-unused `java.lang.reflect.Constructor` imports from XmlParser, PropertiesParser and YamlParser after delegating to PropertyFactory.
output_json.risk_notes: Behavior change: constructing a flip-strategy or property with a class name that resolves but does not implement/extend the expected base type now fails fast with IllegalArgumentException/FeatureAccessException instead of the previous (also-failing, but post-construction) ClassCastException path — net effect is identical for legitimate configs (which always name a proper FlippingStrategy/Property subclass) and only changes behavior for malicious/malformed input, which is the intended fix. Ran full ff4j-core (1125 tests), ff4j-config-properties, ff4j-config-yaml, ff4j-web, and ff4j-utils-json test suites in the project Docker image — all green, 0 failures/errors. Re-ran the provided POV after the patch: it now prints 'NOT VULNERABLE' and exits 1 (previously exited 0/'VULNERABLE'). Two new regression tests added (MappingUtilsTest.testInstanceFlippingStrategyRejectsForeignClassBeforeConstruction, MappingUtilsTest.testLoadClassRejectsClassNotAssignableToExpectedType, PropertyFactoryTest.testCreatePropertyRejectsForeignClassBeforeConstruction) directly assert, via a static side-effect flag, that the attacker-named class's constructor never runs — mirroring the POV's own verification technique in the project's normal JUnit suite.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-094 unchecked reflective construction (Class.forName(...).newInstance()/Constructor.newInstance()) at every source-to-sink path named in the alert: flip-strategy loading (MappingUtil, XmlParser, PropertiesParser, YamlParser, ConsoleOperations) and property-type loading (PropertyFactory, XmlParser, PropertiesParser, YamlParser), plus the JSON parsers and Mongo mapper which already funneled through PropertyFactory/MappingUtil. Added a shared MappingUtil.loadClass(className, expectedType) helper that resolves the class and enforces expectedType.isAssignableFrom(rawClazz) BEFORE any constructor runs, throwing IllegalArgumentException otherwise. All flip-strategy sinks now call MappingUtil.loadClass(name, FlippingStrategy.class); PropertyFactory.createProperty now calls MappingUtil.loadClass(pType, Property.class) before getConstructor/newInstance. The duplicate inline Class.forName(...).getConstructor(...).newInstance(...) logic in XmlParser, PropertiesParser and YamlParser for property types was removed and replaced with a delegate to the now-hardened PropertyFactory.createProperty, eliminating the duplicated unguarded sinks rather than patching each copy separately.
